summary: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, 5.7 Integrals Resulting in Inverse Trigonometric Functions: Integrate functions resulting in inverse trigonometric functions
body: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section "5.7 Integrals Resulting in Inverse Trigonometric Functions", prints these objectives: "Integrate functions resulting in inverse trigonometric functions". The section text says: "In this section we focus on integrals that result in inverse trigonometric functions. We have worked with these functions before. Recall from Functions and Graphs that trigonometric functions are not one-to-one unless the domains are restricted. When working with inverses of trigonometric functions, we always need to be careful to take these restrictions into account. Also in Derivatives , we developed formulas for derivatives of inverse trigonometric functions. The formulas developed there…" This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
